Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the weekly session called the "Open Door" session, the ninety-ninth of them. This session takes place on Thursday, the fourteenth of Rabi' al-Awwal, in the year one thousand four hundred and sixteen (after the Hijrah), and in it we discuss, by the will of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, the tafsir of Surat al-'Asr.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿By time, indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ [al-'Asr 1-2]. So what is meant by al-'Asr?

It has been said that al-'Asr means the end of the day, because the end of the day is its best part, and the Prayer of 'Asr is called the "middle prayer" (al-Salat al-Wusta), i.e., the most excellent (al-Fudhla), as the Prophet (ﷺ) named it.

And it has been said that al-'Asr is time in general, and this is the more correct view: that al-'Asr is time, which Allah swore by because of the variation of conditions that occurs in it, the fluctuations of affairs, and the alternation of days among people, and other things that are witnessed in the present and reported about in the past. So al-'Asr is the time in which creation lives, and its periods vary in hardship and ease, in war and peace, in health and sickness, in righteous deeds and evil deeds, and other things that are known to all.

What did Allah swear by it for? For His saying: ﴿indeed, mankind is in loss﴾. The word "mankind" (al-Insan) here is general, because what is meant by it is the genus. The sign of a generic noun that is intended as a general term is that the word "kull" (all) can take the place of the definite article "al", so here, if one said "kullu insanin fi khusr" (every human being is in loss), that would be the meaning.

The meaning of the noble verse is that Allah swore an oath concerning the state of man, that he is in loss, i.e., in ruin and deficiency in all his states, in this world and in the Hereafter, except for those whom Allah the Mighty and Majestic excludes. This sentence, as you see, is emphasized by three emphases: the first is the oath; the second is ﴿inna﴾; the third is the lam. He said ﴿la-fi khusr﴾ so that it would be more eloquent than saying "la-khasir" (surely a loser). That is because "fi" — what is its meaning? Its meaning is that of containment, so it is as if man is immersed in loss, and loss encompasses him from every side.

﴿Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and enjoin one another to truth, and enjoin one another to patience﴾ [al-'Asr 3]. Allah the Exalted excepted those who possess these four attributes. The first attribute: faith that is not mixed with doubt or hesitation. In what? In what the Messenger (ﷺ) explained when Jibril asked him about faith. He said: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and that you believe in the divine decree, its good and its evil." [Narrated by Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.] The explanation of this hadith would be lengthy if we discussed it now, but we have discussed it in many places. Those who believe in these six foundations are the believers, but it must be a faith with no doubt or hesitation in it; meaning that you believe in these things as though you were seeing them with your own eyes.

People in this regard are of three categories:
The first category: a believer who is sincere, with a faith in which there is no doubt or hesitation.
The second category: a disbelieving, denying rejecter.
The third category: the wavering one.

Which of these three categories is saved? The one who is saved is the first category, who believes with faith without hesitation. He believes in Allah: in His existence, His names, His attributes, His divinity and His lordship, and other things that are known of the attributes of the Lord, Majestic and Exalted. He believes in the angels, who are an unseen world. Allah created them from light and assigned them tasks, some of which are known and some of which are not known. Jibril, upon him be prayer and peace, is charged with revelation, which he brings down from Allah to the prophets and messengers; Mika'il is charged with rain and plants — meaning Allah entrusted him with rain and everything related to rain, and with plants; Israfil is entrusted with blowing the Trumpet; Malik is entrusted with the Fire; Ridwan is entrusted with Paradise. Among the angels are those whose names we do not know and whose deeds we also do not know. But there came in a hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) that "there is no place of four fingers' breadth in the heavens except that there is an angel standing for Allah, or bowing, or prostrating." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2312) from the hadith of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I see what you do not see, and I hear what you do not hear. The heaven has creaked, and it has the right to creak; there is not a place of four fingers in it except that an angel is placing his forehead in prostration to Allah. By Allah, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much, and you would not enjoy women on beds, and you would go out to the high roads crying out to Allah." I wish I had been a tree that is cut down. The phrase "I wish I had been a tree that is cut down" is from the words of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him; see Musnad Ahmad (21516).]

Likewise we believe in the books that Allah sent down to the messengers, upon them be prayer and peace, and we believe in the messengers. Those whom Allah has related to us we believe in by their names, and those whom He has not related to us we believe in generally, because Allah has not related to us all the accounts of the messengers. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Among them are those We have related to you, and among them are those We have not related to you﴾ [Ghafir 78].

The Last Day is the Day of Resurrection, the day on which people come out of their graves for recompense, "barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, and destitute" [Narrated by al-Bukhari (3349) and Muslim (2860/58), with their chains, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us giving a sermon with an exhortation and said: "O people, indeed you will be gathered to Allah barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us; indeed We are ever doing it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 104] ..." The hadith. As for the word "destitute" (buhman), it came in what Ahmad (16042) narrated from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Unays, may Allah be pleased with him, in which it says: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection — or he said: the servants — naked, uncircumcised, destitute."]. So "barefoot" (huffa) means those who have no sandals or shoes; that is, their feet are bare. "Naked" ('uraa) means those who have no clothes. "Uncircumcised" (ghurl) means those who have not been circumcised. "Destitute" (buhm) means those who have no wealth. Thus they will be gathered. When the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned that they would be naked, 'Aishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, do men and women look at one another?" He said: "The matter is greater than that" [Narrated by al-Bukhari (6527) and Muslim (2859/56), with their chains, to 'Aishah who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, men and women all together, do they look at one another?" He (ﷺ) said: "O 'Aishah, the matter is too severe for them to look at one another." As for the word "destitute" (buhman), it came in what Ahmad (16042) narrated from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Unays, may Allah be pleased with him, in which it says: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection — or he said: the servants — naked, uncircumcised, destitute."]; that is, the matter is too great for them to look at one another, because each person is preoccupied with himself.

Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Among faith in the Last Day is belief in everything the Prophet (ﷺ) informed about that will happen after death. So it is obligatory to believe in the trial of the grave, that is, the test that the deceased undergoes when he is buried and his companions turn away from him: two angels come to him and ask him about his Lord, his religion, and his Prophet [Narrated by Abu Dawud (4753) with his chain from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for the funeral of a man from the Ansar, and we reached the grave before it had been dug, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat down and we sat around him as if birds were on our heads, and he had a stick with which he was scratching the ground. He raised his head and said: "Seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the grave" twice or three times. ... and he said: "Indeed he hears the sound of their sandals when they turn away and leave him, when it is said to him: O so-and-so, who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet? ..." The hadith.]. And you believe also that the grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire [Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (8613) with his chain from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The grave is a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire."]; that is, in it there is either punishment or reward. You also believe in Paradise and Hell, and everything related to the Last Day is included in our saying: that you believe in Allah and the Last Day.

Qadar: the decree of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. That is, it is obligatory to believe that Allah the Exalted has decreed everything. This is because "Allah created the Pen and said to it: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write what will exist until the Day of Resurrection" [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2155) from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording is: "Indeed the first thing Allah created was the Pen. He said to it: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write the decree of what has been and what will be until eternity."]. Thus, at that moment, what will exist until the Day of Resurrection was written.

So, the faith in His saying ﴿except those who believe﴾ includes what? It includes faith in the six foundations that the Messenger (ﷺ) explained.

As for His saying ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, its meaning is that they performed righteous deeds: prayer, zakah, fasting, Hajj, kindness to parents, maintaining ties of kinship, and other things. They did not limit themselves to what is merely in the heart, but acted and produced.

Righteous deeds are those that include two things: the first is sincerity to Allah, and the second is following the Messenger (ﷺ). That is because an deed that is not sincerely for Allah is rejected. Allah, blessed and exalted, said in the sacred hadith that the Prophet (ﷺ) narrates from Him: Allah said: "I am the most free of partners from association. Whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I leave him and his association." [Narrated by Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.] So if you stand to pray to be seen by people, or give charity to be seen by people, or seek knowledge to be seen by people, or maintain ties of kinship to be seen by people, or other such things, the deed is rejected even if it is righteous in its outward appearance.

Likewise, following: if you do a deed that the Messenger (ﷺ) did not do, and draw near to Allah by it along with sincerity to Allah, it will not be accepted from you, because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our matter, it is rejected." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) in similar wording, and Muslim (1718/18) with his wording, from the hadith of 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]

So righteous deeds are those that combine two qualities: the first is sincerity to Allah, and the second is following the Messenger (ﷺ).

﴿And enjoin one another to truth﴾: that is, some of them began to advise others to truth, and truth is the Shari'ah. That is, each of them advises the other: if he sees him neglecting an obligation, he advises him; he says: "O brother, benefit yourself, perform the duty." If he sees him committing something forbidden, he advises him; he says: "O brother, avoid what is unlawful." They did not limit themselves to benefiting themselves, but benefited themselves and others. ﴿Enjoined one another to truth﴾: here, truth means what? The Shari'ah, which they advise one another to follow.

﴿And enjoin one another to patience﴾. Patience is restraining the self from what should not be done. The scholars divided it into three categories, saying: patience is patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from what Allah has forbidden, and patience in the decrees of Allah; three categories.

Patience in obedience: many people have laziness about praying in congregation, for example. He does not go to the mosque, saying: "I pray at home and I have fulfilled the obligation," so he is lazy. We say: "O brother, be patient with yourself; restrain it, compel it to pray in congregation."

Many people, when they see the zakah of their wealth is large, become miserly and stingy and begin to hesitate: "Shall I pay out this large amount of money, or leave it, or later I'll see?" and similar things. We say: "O brother, be patient with yourself; compel it to pay zakah."

And likewise with the rest of the acts of worship, for acts of worship, as Allah the Exalted said regarding prayer: ﴿And indeed, it is difficult except for the humble﴾ [al-Baqarah 45]. You find that most of Allah's servants find acts of worship burdensome, so they enjoin one another to patience: "Be patient in obedience; do not become weary, do not be lazy."

Likewise patience in refraining from sin: some people are dragged by their souls toward unlawful earnings, whether through usury, or through cheating and lying, or through fraud, or other kinds of what is forbidden. So we say: "O brother, be patient, be patient with yourself; do not deal in a forbidden manner."

Some people are also afflicted with looking at women. You find him walking in the market, and whenever a woman passes he follows her with his gaze. We say: "O brother, be patient, restrain yourself from this thing."

Patience in the decrees of Allah: a person is afflicted with illness in his body; a person is afflicted with the loss of some of his wealth; a person is afflicted with the loss of his loved ones, and he becomes distressed, resentful and pained. So they enjoin one another: "O brother, be patient. This is a predetermined matter, and distress does not benefit anything, and prolonged sorrow does not remove sorrow. Be patient, consider that this thing never existed at all." For example, a person who lost a million riyals grieves over it and is tormented by it: what do we say to him? We say: "O brother, be patient, consider that this million never existed. Did you not come out of your mother's womb with no clothes on?! Consider that this never was."

Likewise with children: for example, a person tested by the death of his son. We say: "O brother, be patient, consider that this son was never created." Then, as the Messenger (ﷺ) said to one of his daughters: "Tell her to be patient and seek reward; for to Allah belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He gives" [Narrated by al-Bukhari (7448) and Muslim (923/11), with their chains, from Usamah ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ), when one of his daughters sent to him calling him and informing him that a child of hers, or a son of hers, was dying. He said to the messenger: "Return to her and inform her that to Allah belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He gives, and everything with Him has a specified term. So tell her to be patient and seek reward ..." The hadith.]. The whole matter belongs to Allah, not to you. So when Allah the Exalted takes back His possession, how can you blame your Lord?! How can you be resentful?!

These are the types of patience: the first is patience in obedience to Allah, the second is patience in refraining from disobedience to Allah, and the third is patience in the decrees of Allah.

Which of them is hardest on the souls? This varies. Some people find performing acts of obedience difficult and very burdensome, and for others it is the opposite: obedience is easy for them, but refraining from sin is hard and very difficult. And some people find it easy to be patient in obedience and patient in refraining from sin, but cannot bear patience in calamities; they are unable, and may reach the point of apostasy — may Allah protect us — as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge; if good touches him, he is reassured by it, but if an trial strikes him, he turns back on his face; he has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss﴾ [al-Hajj 11].

So from this verse we derive that Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, emphasized with an oath and with the emphatic particles "inna" and the lam that all of mankind are, what? Losers. Rather, they are in loss; loss encompasses them from every side, except for those who possess these four qualities: faith, righteous deeds, mutual exhortation to truth, and mutual exhortation to patience.

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Had Allah sent down to His servants no proof except this surah, it would have sufficed them." That is, it would have sufficed them as a admonition, not as legislation, because there is nothing in it of legislation: there is no purification, no prayer, no zakat, no pilgrimage, and no fasting in it. But it suffices them as an admonition. Every intelligent person knows that he is in loss unless he possesses these four qualities, and then he will strive, to the extent he is able, to acquire these four qualities.

We ask Allah to make us and you among the winners who are granted success.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

That is, each of them advises the other: if he sees him neglecting an obligation, he advises him; he says: "O brother, benefit yourself, perform the duty." If he sees him committing something forbidden, he advises him; he says: "O brother, avoid what is unlawful." They did not limit themselves to benefiting themselves, but benefited themselves and others. ﴿Enjoined one another to truth﴾: here, truth means what? The Shari'ah, which they advise one another to follow.

﴿And enjoin one another to patience﴾. Patience is restraining the self from what should not be done. The scholars divided it into three categories, saying: patience is patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from what Allah has forbidden, and patience in the decrees of Allah; three categories.

Patience in obedience: many people have laziness about praying in congregation, for example. He does not go to the mosque, saying: "I pray at home and I have fulfilled the obligation," so he is lazy. We say: "O brother, be patient with yourself; restrain it, compel it to pray in congregation."

Many people, when they see the zakah of their wealth is large, become miserly and stingy and begin to hesitate: "Shall I pay out this large amount of money, or leave it, or later I'll see?" and similar things. We say: "O brother, be patient with yourself; compel it to pay zakah."

And likewise with the rest of the acts of worship, for acts of worship, as Allah the Exalted said regarding prayer: ﴿And indeed, it is difficult except for the humble﴾ [al-Baqarah 45]. You find that most of Allah's servants find acts of worship burdensome, so they enjoin one another to patience: "Be patient in obedience; do not become weary, do not be lazy."

Likewise patience in refraining from sin: some people are dragged by their souls toward unlawful earnings, whether through usury, or through cheating and lying, or through fraud, or other kinds of what is forbidden. So we say: "O brother, be patient, be patient with yourself; do not deal in a forbidden manner."

Some people are also afflicted with looking at women. You find him walking in the market, and whenever a woman passes he follows her with his gaze. We say: "O brother, be patient, restrain yourself from this thing."

Patience in the decrees of Allah: a person is afflicted with illness in his body; a person is afflicted with the loss of some of his wealth; a person is afflicted with the loss of his loved ones, and he becomes distressed, resentful and pained. So they enjoin one another: "O brother, be patient. This is a predetermined matter, and distress does not benefit anything, and prolonged sorrow does not remove sorrow. Be patient, consider that this thing never existed at all." For example, a person who lost a million riyals grieves over it and is tormented by it: what do we say to him? We say: "O brother, be patient, consider that this million never existed. Did you not come out of your mother's womb with no clothes on?! Consider that this never was."

Likewise with children: for example, a person tested by the death of his son. We say: "O brother, be patient, consider that this son was never created." Then, as the Messenger (ﷺ) said to one of his daughters: "Tell her to be patient and seek reward; for to Allah belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He gives" [Narrated by al-Bukhari (7448) and Muslim (923/11), with their chains, from Usamah ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ), when one of his daughters sent to him calling him and informing him that a child of hers, or a son of hers, was dying. He said to the messenger: "Return to her and inform her that to Allah belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He gives, and everything with Him has a specified term. So tell her to be patient and seek reward ..." The hadith.]. The whole matter belongs to Allah, not to you. So when Allah the Exalted takes back His possession, how can you blame your Lord?! How can you be resentful?!

These are the types of patience: the first is patience in obedience to Allah, the second is patience in refraining from disobedience to Allah, and the third is patience in the decrees of Allah.

Which of them is hardest on the souls? This varies. Some people find performing acts of obedience difficult and very burdensome, and for others it is the opposite: obedience is easy for them, but refraining from sin is hard and very difficult. And some people find it easy to be patient in obedience and patient in refraining from sin, but cannot bear patience in calamities; they are unable, and may reach the point of apostasy — may Allah protect us — as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge; if good touches him, he is reassured by it, but if an trial strikes him, he turns back on his face; he has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss﴾ [al-Hajj 11].

So from this verse we derive that Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, emphasized with an oath and with the emphatic particles "inna" and the lam that all of mankind are, what? Losers. Rather, they are in loss; loss encompasses them from every side, except for those who possess these four qualities: faith, righteous deeds, mutual exhortation to truth, and mutual exhortation to patience.

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Had Allah sent down to His servants no proof except this surah, it would have sufficed them." That is, it would have sufficed them as a admonition, not as legislation, because there is nothing in it of legislation: there is no purification, no prayer, no zakat, no pilgrimage, and no fasting in it. But it suffices them as an admonition. Every intelligent person knows that he is in loss unless he possesses these four qualities, and then he will strive, to the extent he is able, to acquire these four qualities.

We ask Allah to make us and you among the winners who are granted success.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the weekly session called the "Open Door" session, the ninety-ninth of them. This session takes place on Thursday, the fourteenth of Rabi' al-Awwal, in the year one thousand four hundred and sixteen (after the Hijrah), and in it we discuss, by the will of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, the tafsir of Surat al-'Asr.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿By time, indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ [al-'Asr 1-2]. So what is meant by al-'Asr?

It has been said that al-'Asr means the end of the day, because the end of the day is its best part, and the Prayer of 'Asr is called the "middle prayer" (al-Salat al-Wusta), i.e., the most excellent (al-Fudhla), as the Prophet (ﷺ) named it.

And it has been said that al-'Asr is time in general, and this is the more correct view: that al-'Asr is time, which Allah swore by because of the variation of conditions that occurs in it, the fluctuations of affairs, and the alternation of days among people, and other things that are witnessed in the present and reported about in the past. So al-'Asr is the time in which creation lives, and its periods vary in hardship and ease, in war and peace, in health and sickness, in righteous deeds and evil deeds, and other things that are known to all.

What did Allah swear by it for? For His saying: ﴿indeed, mankind is in loss﴾. The word "mankind" (al-Insan) here is general, because what is meant by it is the genus. The sign of a generic noun that is intended as a general term is that the word "kull" (all) can take the place of the definite article "al", so here, if one said "kullu insanin fi khusr" (every human being is in loss), that would be the meaning.

The meaning of the noble verse is that Allah swore an oath concerning the state of man, that he is in loss, i.e., in ruin and deficiency in all his states, in this world and in the Hereafter, except for those whom Allah the Mighty and Majestic excludes. This sentence, as you see, is emphasized by three emphases: the first is the oath; the second is ﴿inna﴾; the third is the lam. He said ﴿la-fi khusr﴾ so that it would be more eloquent than saying "la-khasir" (surely a loser). That is because "fi" — what is its meaning? Its meaning is that of containment, so it is as if man is immersed in loss, and loss encompasses him from every side.

﴿Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and enjoin one another to truth, and enjoin one another to patience﴾ [al-'Asr 3]. Allah the Exalted excepted those who possess these four attributes. The first attribute: faith that is not mixed with doubt or hesitation. In what? In what the Messenger (ﷺ) explained when Jibril asked him about faith. He said: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and that you believe in the divine decree, its good and its evil." [Narrated by Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.] The explanation of this hadith would be lengthy if we discussed it now, but we have discussed it in many places. Those who believe in these six foundations are the believers, but it must be a faith with no doubt or hesitation in it; meaning that you believe in these things as though you were seeing them with your own eyes.

People in this regard are of three categories:
The first category: a believer who is sincere, with a faith in which there is no doubt or hesitation.
The second category: a disbelieving, denying rejecter.
The third category: the wavering one.

Which of these three categories is saved? The one who is saved is the first category, who believes with faith without hesitation. He believes in Allah: in His existence, His names, His attributes, His divinity and His lordship, and other things that are known of the attributes of the Lord, Majestic and Exalted. He believes in the angels, who are an unseen world. Allah created them from light and assigned them tasks, some of which are known and some of which are not known. Jibril, upon him be prayer and peace, is charged with revelation, which he brings down from Allah to the prophets and messengers; Mika'il is charged with rain and plants — meaning Allah entrusted him with rain and everything related to rain, and with plants; Israfil is entrusted with blowing the Trumpet; Malik is entrusted with the Fire; Ridwan is entrusted with Paradise. Among the angels are those whose names we do not know and whose deeds we also do not know. But there came in a hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) that "there is no place of four fingers' breadth in the heavens except that there is an angel standing for Allah, or bowing, or prostrating." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2312) from the hadith of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I see what you do not see, and I hear what you do not hear. The heaven has creaked, and it has the right to creak; there is not a place of four fingers in it except that an angel is placing his forehead in prostration to Allah. By Allah, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much, and you would not enjoy women on beds, and you would go out to the high roads crying out to Allah." I wish I had been a tree that is cut down. The phrase "I wish I had been a tree that is cut down" is from the words of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him; see Musnad Ahmad (21516).]

Likewise we believe in the books that Allah sent down to the messengers, upon them be prayer and peace, and we believe in the messengers. Those whom Allah has related to us we believe in by their names, and those whom He has not related to us we believe in generally, because Allah has not related to us all the accounts of the messengers. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Among them are those We have related to you, and among them are those We have not related to you﴾ [Ghafir 78].

The Last Day is the Day of Resurrection, the day on which people come out of their graves for recompense, "barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, and destitute" [Narrated by al-Bukhari (3349) and Muslim (2860/58), with their chains, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us giving a sermon with an exhortation and said: "O people, indeed you will be gathered to Allah barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us; indeed We are ever doing it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 104] ..." The hadith. As for the word "destitute" (buhman), it came in what Ahmad (16042) narrated from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Unays, may Allah be pleased with him, in which it says: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection — or he said: the servants — naked, uncircumcised, destitute."]. So "barefoot" (huffa) means those who have no sandals or shoes; that is, their feet are bare. "Naked" ('uraa) means those who have no clothes. "Uncircumcised" (ghurl) means those who have not been circumcised. "Destitute" (buhm) means those who have no wealth. Thus they will be gathered. When the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned that they would be naked, 'Aishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, do men and women look at one another?" He said: "The matter is greater than that" [Narrated by al-Bukhari (6527) and Muslim (2859/56), with their chains, to 'Aishah who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, men and women all together, do they look at one another?" He (ﷺ) said: "O 'Aishah, the matter is too severe for them to look at one another." As for the word "destitute" (buhman), it came in what Ahmad (16042) narrated from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Unays, may Allah be pleased with him, in which it says: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection — or he said: the servants — naked, uncircumcised, destitute."]; that is, the matter is too great for them to look at one another, because each person is preoccupied with himself.

Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Among faith in the Last Day is belief in everything the Prophet (ﷺ) informed about that will happen after death. So it is obligatory to believe in the trial of the grave, that is, the test that the deceased undergoes when he is buried and his companions turn away from him: two angels come to him and ask him about his Lord, his religion, and his Prophet [Narrated by Abu Dawud (4753) with his chain from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for the funeral of a man from the Ansar, and we reached the grave before it had been dug, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat down and we sat around him as if birds were on our heads, and he had a stick with which he was scratching the ground. He raised his head and said: "Seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the grave" twice or three times. ... and he said: "Indeed he hears the sound of their sandals when they turn away and leave him, when it is said to him: O so-and-so, who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet? ..." The hadith.]. And you believe also that the grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire [Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (8613) with his chain from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The grave is a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire."]; that is, in it there is either punishment or reward. You also believe in Paradise and Hell, and everything related to the Last Day is included in our saying: that you believe in Allah and the Last Day.

Qadar: the decree of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. That is, it is obligatory to believe that Allah the Exalted has decreed everything. This is because "Allah created the Pen and said to it: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write what will exist until the Day of Resurrection" [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2155) from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording is: "Indeed the first thing Allah created was the Pen. He said to it: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write the decree of what has been and what will be until eternity."]. Thus, at that moment, what will exist until the Day of Resurrection was written.

So, the faith in His saying ﴿except those who believe﴾ includes what? It includes faith in the six foundations that the Messenger (ﷺ) explained.

As for His saying ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, its meaning is that they performed righteous deeds: prayer, zakah, fasting, Hajj, kindness to parents, maintaining ties of kinship, and other things. They did not limit themselves to what is merely in the heart, but acted and produced.

Righteous deeds are those that include two things: the first is sincerity to Allah, and the second is following the Messenger (ﷺ). That is because an deed that is not sincerely for Allah is rejected. Allah, blessed and exalted, said in the sacred hadith that the Prophet (ﷺ) narrates from Him: Allah said: "I am the most free of partners from association. Whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I leave him and his association." [Narrated by Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.] So if you stand to pray to be seen by people, or give charity to be seen by people, or seek knowledge to be seen by people, or maintain ties of kinship to be seen by people, or other such things, the deed is rejected even if it is righteous in its outward appearance.

Likewise, following: if you do a deed that the Messenger (ﷺ) did not do, and draw near to Allah by it along with sincerity to Allah, it will not be accepted from you, because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our matter, it is rejected." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) in similar wording, and Muslim (1718/18) with his wording, from the hadith of 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]

So righteous deeds are those that combine two qualities: the first is sincerity to Allah, and the second is following the Messenger (ﷺ).
